questions.question: Find the volume of a cylinder (in cm³) if its area of the base is 1,386 cm² and its height is 30 cm.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area of base (circle) of the cylinder = 1386 cm²

Height (h) of the cylinder = 30 cm

**Formula used: **

Cylinder volume = π x (radius)² x height 

Area of the circle = π x (radius)² [Radius (r)] 

**Calculation: **

Area of the circle = π x (radius)² 

⇒ 1386 = π x (r)² …......(1) 

⇒ Volume of the cylinder = π x (r)² x height …....(2) 

From (1) and (2) we get, 

⇒ Volume = 1386 x h 

⇒ Volume = 1386 x 30 = 41580 cm³

**∴ The volume of a cylinder (in cm3) is 41580 cm3.**

questions.question: Each cell of a memory device is capable of storing one bit of information in the form of binary numbers. What does the term 'bit' mean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Binary digit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Binary digit (bit)**

 
 
• The **smallest unit** of data that a computer can process and store is a bit **(binary digit)**.
 
• Similar to an **on/off **light switch, a bit is always in one of two physical states.
 
• Usually a **0 or 1**, the state is represented by a **single binary integer**.
 
• However, **yes/no, on/off, or true/false** can also be used to describe the state.
 
• **Capacitors** are used to store bits in memory because they can store electrical charges.
 
• Each bit's state, which in turn determines its value, is determined by the charge.
 
• **The majority of systems, process and store data in bytes**, even if a computer may be able to evaluate and alter data at the bit level.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **byte** is an **eight-bit string **that is regarded as a single unit.
 
• **How bits work **
 
 
• The **place value**, also known as the bit value, is the value that is assigned to each bit in a byte.
 
• Based on the individual bits of a byte, the place values are utilised to explain the meaning of the byte as a whole.
 
• Each bit is given a place value in a** right-to-left pattern**, with the value starting at **1 **and **increasing by doubling **for each bit.

questions.question: _________ is a strait between the Tamil Nadu state of India and the Jaffna District of the Northern Province of the island nation of Sri Lanka.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Palk Strait** 

 
 
• It is a strait between the **Tamil Nadu state of India** and the **Jaffna District of the Northern Province of the island nation of Sri Lanka**.
 
• **Sri Lanka** and** India** are separated by the **Palk Strait**.
 
• The **Gulf of Mannar, Pamban Island (India), Adam's (Rama's) Bridge (a chain of shoals), and Mannar Island (Sri Lanka)** surrounds it on the south (Sri Lanka).
 
• **Palk Bay** is another name for the strait's western portion.
 
• The strait is less than **330 feet (100 metres) deep, 40 to 85 miles (64 to 137 km) long, and 64 to 137 km wide**.
 
• On the Sri Lankan side, it contains many islands and various **rivers**, including the **Vaigai** (India).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Robert Palk**, a governor of Madras from **1755 to 1763** during the Company Raj era, is honoured by the strait's name.
 
• Palk Strait is distinct because of the **high contrast between the waves to its north and south**.
 
• The waves in the **Bay of Bengal are primarily swelled to the north**, while the waves in Palk Bay are primarily sea waves to the south.
 
• Despite being heavily influenced by the sea, Palk Bay locations have comparatively **small notable wave heights**.

questions.question: Five bells commence tolling together and toll at intervals of 3, 6, 12, 15 and 18 seconds respectively. They tolled at 9:58:45 hours then at which time they will again toll together?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of the given intervals: 3, 6, 12, 15, and 18 seconds.

**LCM**(3, 6, 12, 15, 18) = **180 seconds**.

Convert 180 seconds to minutes → 180 ÷ 60 = **3 minutes**.

Next tolling time = Initial time + **LCM** = 9:58:45 + 3 minutes = **10:01:45**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:01:45.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Intervals of tolling: **3 sec, 6 sec, 12 sec, 15 sec, 18 sec**.

First tolling time: **9:58:45 hr**.

**Formula Used:**

The time after which all bells will toll together is the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of their individual tolling intervals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f21ae8c4b9663437740ad5618c1ee8fd82bb612bd99695933df026cec5efe6c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of intervals:

⇒ 3 = 3¹

⇒ 6 = 2¹ × 3¹

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3¹

⇒ 15 = 3¹ × 5¹

⇒ 18 = 2¹ × 3²

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 3² × 5¹ = 4 × 9 × 5 = **180 seconds**.

⇒ Convert 180 seconds to minutes: 180 ÷ 60 = **3 minutes**.

⇒ Add 3 minutes to the initial time (9:58:45):

⇒ 9:58:45 + 0:03:00 = **10:01:45**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:01:45.**

**__Additional Information__**

Application of LCM

**LCM** is used to find the next simultaneous occurrence of events that happen at fixed periodic intervals, such as bells tolling or traffic lights changing.

Time Conversion Rules

questions.question: The number of students in grades 10, 11 and 12 of a school are 348, 256 and 480 respectively. All students were divided into different groups, with no group having students from more than one grade. What is the minimum number of groups that would be formed if all the groups have the same number of students?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number of students in grades 10 = 348

The number of students in grades 11 = 256 

The number of students in grades 12 = 480 

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

Maximum no. of students in each group = HCF of all grades

⇒ HCF of grade 10 = 348 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 29

⇒ HCF of grade 11 = 256 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 

⇒ HCF of grade 12 = 480 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5

HCF of (348, 256, 480) = 4

Now no. of group in grade 10

⇒ (No. of students)/(No. of students in each group)

⇒ 348/4 = 87

⇒ Now no. of group in grade 11 = 256/4 = 64

⇒ Now no. of group in grade 12 = 480/4 = 120

Now total no. of groups 

⇒ 120 + 87 + 64 = 271

**∴ The minimum number of groups that would be formed is 271.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the lowermost layer of the earth's atmosphere?
questions.solution:

**Troposphere**

__
 
• **The lowest layer of our atmosphere is called the troposphere.**
 
• It begins at ground level and rises to a height of approximately **10 kilometers (6.2 miles or 33,000 feet) above sea level.**
 
• Nearly** all weather occurs in the troposphere**, where we people reside.
 
• Because the troposphere contains 99 percent of the atmosphere's water vapor, this is where the majority of clouds form.​

**Stratosphere**

 
• From the** troposphere** to** roughly 50 km (31 miles) above the surface,** the stratosphere is present.
 
• The stratosphere **contains the protective ozone layer.**
 
• High-intensity ultraviolet (UV) light from the Sun is absorbed by ozone molecules in this layer, which turns the UV energy into heat. 

**Mesosphere**

 
• The** mesosphere is located above the stratosphere.**
 
• It rises to an altitude of** roughly 85 km (53 miles) above our planet.**
 
• The mesosphere is where most meteors burn up. As you ascend through the mesosphere, temperatures drop once more, in contrast to the stratosphere.

**Thermosphere**

 
• **The thermosphere refers to the layer of extremely rare air above the mesosphere.**
 
• The thermosphere heats up to hundreds or even thousands of degrees as a result of the Sun's high-energy X-rays and UV radiation being absorbed there.

questions.question: If 13.5 kg of grapes cost Rs. 681.75, find the cost of 12 kg of grapes.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **unitary method** directly:

Cost of 13.5 kg = Rs. 681.75

Cost of 12 kg = (681.75 ÷ 13.5) × 12

Cost of 12 kg = 50.5 × 12 = 606

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 606.00.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity 1 (Q₁) = **13.5 kg**

Cost 1 (C₁) = **Rs. 681.75**

Quantity 2 (Q₂) = **12 kg**

**Formula Used:**

Since cost is **directly proportional** to weight: C₁ ÷ Q₁ = C₂ ÷ Q₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08ae8d7f2fefb27dfbb6d6dbbd2c7c8b131e7ad0eb2284773ee1a736f4082008.png] 

⇒ Cost of 1 kg grapes = 681.75 ÷ 13.5

⇒ Cost of 1 kg grapes = 68175 ÷ 1350

⇒ Cost of 1 kg grapes = 50.5

⇒ Cost of 12 kg grapes = 50.5 × 12

⇒ Cost of 12 kg grapes = 606

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 606.00.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method Concept

The **unitary method** is a technique for solving problems by first finding the value of a **single unit**, and then finding the necessary value by multiplying the single unit value.

Direct Variation

When two quantities are related such that as one increases, the other also increases at the same rate, they are in **direct variation**. The ratio Cost/Weight remains constant.

Calculation Tip

To simplify decimals, multiply both the numerator and denominator by a power of 10 (e.g., 681.75/13.5 = 68175/1350) before performing **division**.</p

questions.question: Which of the numbers below is not divisible by 15?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is **divisible by 15** if it is divisible by both **3** and **5**.

All options end in 0 or 5, so all are **divisible by 5**.

Check **divisibility by 3**: The sum of digits must be a multiple of 3.

For 384575: 3 + 8 + 4 + 5 + 7 + 5 = 32 (32 is not divisible by 3).

**∴ The correct answer is 384575.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Numbers:** 123465, 234675, 234570, 384575

**Formula:** 15 = 3 × 5. A number is divisible by 15 if it is divisible by **co-prime** factors 3 and 5.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/239dd42f0d6af1888cd276124e9f70817185f9b2422019fcf7f679964ebf365e.png] 

**Step-by-step verification:**

⇒ **Option 1 (123465):** Last digit is 5. Sum = 1+2+3+4+6+5 = 21. Since 21 ÷ 3 = 7, it is divisible by 15.

⇒ **Option 2 (234675):** Last digit is 5. Sum = 2+3+4+6+7+5 = 27. Since 27 ÷ 3 = 9, it is divisible by 15.

⇒ **Option 3 (234570):** Last digit is 0. Sum = 2+3+4+5+7+0 = 21. Since 21 ÷ 3 = 7, it is divisible by 15.

⇒ **Option 4 (384575):** Last digit is 5. Sum = 3+8+4+5+7+5 = 32. Since 32 ÷ 3 leaves a **remainder of 2**, it is **not** divisible by 3.

⇒ Since 384575 is not divisible by 3, it cannot be divisible by 15.

**∴ The correct answer is 384575.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 5

A number is divisible by 5 if its **unit digit** (last digit) is either **0 or 5**.

Composite Divisibility

If a number is divisible by two **co-prime** numbers x and y, then it is also divisible by their product (x × y).

Rule for 15

Since 3 and 5 are co-prime, **divisibility by 15** requires fulfilling both rules for 3 and 5 simultaneously.</p

questions.question: A 360 m train crosses an electric pole in 12 seconds. Find the time (in seconds) taken by the train to cross a 150 m long bridge.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the speed of the **Train** is constant, **Time** is directly proportional to **Distance**.

Case 1: Crosses pole → Distance = 360 m → Time = 12 sec

Case 2: Crosses bridge → Distance = 360 + 150 = 510 m

Required Time = (12 ÷ 360) × 510 = 17 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 17 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Speed = 360 ÷ 12 = 30 m/s

⇒ Total distance to cross **Bridge** = Length of Train + Length of Bridge

⇒ Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time taken = 510 ÷ 30 = 17 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 17 sec.**

Time Period = 73/365 = 0.2 year.

**Calculations:**

Simple Interest = 48750 × 16 × 0.2/100 = 156000/100

Simple Interest = 1560 Rs.

**∴ The Simple Interest for 48750 rs at 16% per annum for 73 days is Rs.1560.**

questions.question:
The following chart shows the number of telephone conversations at a Call Centre for various call durations on a particular day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b7a8e64268f8ff7f0eaa205b4c169c12476c80ebf596b27c6c086bd21dff293.png] 

How many minutes of telephone conversations took place on that day?
questions.solution:
**Given : **

On x - axis = minutes of conversation.

On y - axis = number of calls. 

**Calculation : **

First we have to find total no. of minutes for each bar ( a BAR represents no. of calls according to the minutes of conversation).

Total no. of minutes for each bar = no. of minutes × no. of calls. 

For 1 minute conversation = no. of minutes × no. of calls

⇒ 1 × 4 = 4 minutes.

For 2 minute conversation = 2 × 14 = 28 minutes.

For 3 minute conversation = 3 × 40 = 120 minutes.

For 4 minute conversation = 4 × 30 = 120 minutes.

For 5 minute conversation = 5 × 12 = 60 minutes.

To find the total number of minutes of conversations, we have to add all the minutes.​

Total no. of minutes = 4 + 28 + 120 + 120 + 60.

Total no. of minutes = 332 minutes.

**∴ The total no. minutes of telephone conversations that took place on that day is 332 minutes.**
